faq.q: How do I reignite my career without quitting my job?
faq.a: Start by reflecting on what once energized you, then reshape your role, learn something new, and reconnect with your network. Small changes inside your current job can bring back a surprising amount of energy.

faq.q: What are signs my career needs a refresh?
faq.a: Common signs include feeling bored, no longer learning, dreading Mondays, and describing your work as just “fine.” If these last for months, it’s worth paying attention.

faq.q: Is career boredom the same as burnout?
faq.a: Not always. Boredom usually comes from lack of challenge, while burnout comes from prolonged exhaustion. If you’re deeply tired, rest should come before any big career moves.
Job crafting means adjusting your tasks, relationships, and perspective at work to make your role more meaningful. It can be as simple as volunteering for projects that excite you.

faq.q: Which “re” word should I start with?
faq.a: Start with the one that stirs the strongest reaction. Reflect and reassess are good first steps if you’re unsure.

faq.q: How long does it take to feel re-energized at work?
faq.a: It varies. Some people feel a shift within weeks of small changes, while bigger reinventions can take months or longer.
